C0.quote: Liquid democracy is a voting paradigm
C0.note: The paper studies liquid democracy, a procedure aggregating delegated votes into a collective decision, including probabilistic performance properties.

C1.quote: all shown to satisfy do no harm and positive gain
C1.note: Main results are probabilistic performance guarantees for selecting the ground-truth outcome; the paper also proposes new delegation models.

C2.1.value: binary votes Vi and delegation-induced weights weighti(Gn)
C2.1.quote: The binary vote Vi of each voter i is drawn independently

C2.2.quote: Vi = 1 if voter i would vote correctly
C2.2.note: Inputs are binary {0,1} votes and delegation-graph weights, not rankings/approval/cardinal preference scores.

C2.3.quote: Each voter i has a competence level pi
C2.3.note: Competence pi is a held attribute separate from the submitted vote/delegation input.

C2.4.quote: Fixed competencies p~n induce a probability measure Pp~n
C2.4.note: Competencies are separate objects that generate votes probabilistically.

C3.1.quote: our models do not take strategic considerations into account
C3.1.note: No analysis models voters choosing inputs to improve an objective.

C3.2.loc: 2 Model p.5; 1 Introduction p.1; 7 Discussion p.19
C3.2.note: The paper does not state that voters submit their competence or held attitude; votes are random Bernoulli draws.

C4.1.loc: 2 Model p.5; 1 Introduction p.1; 7 Discussion p.19
C4.1.note: C2.2 does not include RANK/WEAK/APPR/DICH/PAIR, and the paper does not use utility/welfare/satisfaction/cost/distortion notions for voters.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: more than half vote for the correct outcome
C5.1.note: Results evaluate probability of selecting the ground truth, not welfare, efficiency, voter utility, representation, proportionality, or distortion.

VOT.quote_behav: With probability 1 − q(pi ) they do not delegate
VOT.note: Voter actions are fixed by probabilistic model, not optimizing. Info is NA because behav is NONSTRAT.

C7.1.quote: There is a set of n voters
C7.1.note: Only voters are present as formal acting agents.

C8.1.quote: our models do not take strategic considerations into account
C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

C9.1.note: Abstract, introduction, and conclusion make claims supporting liquid democracy in practice.

C9.2.quote: Our paper further relies on a set of assumptions
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions for the broad claims include ground truth, independent votes, continuous competence distribution, and no strategic behaviour; these are stated in Section 7.

C10.1.note: No explicit procedural reading found; the paper relates delegated votes and votes to competences.
